text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, removing them from the troponin–tropomyosin complex. This lets tropomyosin block the myosin-binding sites on actin, preventing cross-bridge formation, and the fibre returns to its resting length passively. Relaxation follows once the motor neuron stops releasing acetylcholine and calcium is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
CONFIDENCE: 95
